articleTitle: Speed regulation of a torque-driven pendulum model via a PI based controller
abstract: PID and PI controllers are widely used in industrial processes and control engineering. These controllers require tuning of gains to achieve stability and output regulation. This paper demonstrates the application of a smooth PI controller combined with gravity compensation to regulate the speed of a torque-driven pendulum mechanism, assuming the plant model structure and parameters are known. The analysis uses fundamental concepts from Ordinary Differential Equations and classical control theory to establish tuning rules for speed regulation.

articleTitle: Delivery propofol fault detection in the automation process of general anesthesia
abstract: Given the danger associated with the delivery of anesthesia during general surgical procedures, research in this field has been extensive. The design of controllers to automate the process aims to assist the anesthesiologist in precisely administering the drug dose. Based on the mathematical model of the patient, which is composed of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics models, the automation challenge lies in administering the appropriate drug dose during general surgery, ensuring that the depth of hypnosis remains at a desired value. On the other hand, failures in actuators and monitors are present in the automation process. This article presents an algorithm for detecting a failure in drug infusion pumps. The algorithm for fault detection presented is based on the so-called interval observers and the positivity property of the mathematical dynamic model. The presented model predictive control (MPC) algorithm guarantees the system’s positivity. The proposed algorithm is proven in five in-silico patients where a failure in the infusion pump is simulated and detected.

articleTitle: Neuro-fuzzy trajectory tracking control for the Nexus 4-wheeled omnidirectional mobile robot
abstract: This work presents the design of a single-layer neuro-fuzzy controller to solve the trajectory-tracking problem of an omnidirectional mobile robot with 4 Mecanum wheels. The controller consists of a PD with fuzzy-neural compensation, which does not require knowledge of the plant and is a robust controller that can deal with disturbances. Unlike a conventional neural controller, in the proposed neuro-fuzzy controller a vector of fuzzy products is implemented as the activation function of the neural network. Due to the computational cost that this implies, the controller is designed by subsystems. The neural network weights are updated online using filtered error and adaptive laws. Experimental results are presented on the Nexus 4-wheeled omnidirectional mobile robot, which verify the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Development of an Autonomous Omnidirectional Robot for Obstacle Avoidance Using Potential Fields
abstract: This work presents the development of an omnidirectional mobile robot with four Mecanum wheels, implementing potential fields algorithm for trajectory generation and obstacle avoidance achieving autonomy on our robot. The processing unit is Nvidia Jetson Nano, a single-board computer compatible with Robot Operating System, enabling communication through topics and nodes. Additionally, an ESP32 microcontroller is used for motor control and a LiDAR sensor is incorporated to get information from environment. Communication between the processing unit and nodes through topics ensures efficient data transfer. This combination, along with effective design and construction, aims to develop an autonomous omnidirectional robot capable of obstacle evasion. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the evasion technique used.

articleTitle: LW.Transmech: a family of Leg-Wheel Transformable Mechanisms
abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence, robotics and electromobility make it possible to envision a future with multiple applications for the transportation of goods and people by means of autonomous electric vehicles. This paper present a family of leg-wheel transformable mechanisms for ground vehicles driven by electric actuators. The purpose of these mechanism is to combine the efficiency of the wheels with the ability of the legs to move in complex environments. A comprehensive exploration of the different possible architectures of transformable mechanisms by using different types of joints is performed. Finally some observations about the mobility of these mechanisms are discussed.

articleTitle: Obstacle classifier for ADAS system using Deep Learning
abstract: Summary — This study presents the implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for classifying images within a unique dataset consisting of three categories: pedestrian, infrastructure, and vehicle for an Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) in an electric vehicle. Including preprocessing of the database images, the network achieves an accuracy of 99.83%, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability in image classification. The results highlight the robustness of the architecture and the efficiency of the selected hyperparameters, suggesting its potential for practical applications in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: PID control for a spherical robot applied as a solar tracking system
abstract: This article explores the design and analysis of a spherical solar tracking robot controlled by a PID algorithm. The robot’s spherical shape is used for maximizing solar energy capture. The study utilizes reference signals for both azimuth and altitude angles, offering a more comprehensive and accurate approach to solar tracking compared to previous single-axis and two-axis trackers lacking control systems.The robot’s design was crafted using 3D CAD tools, enabling precise visualization of its geometry and mechanics. Matlab® Simulink and Matlab® Simscape simulations were employed to analyze the PID algorithm. The article delves into the kinematic model of the robot with two degrees of freedom, providing a thorough understanding of its motion and control capabilities.The article concludes with a discussion of the advantages of using a PID-controlled spherical robot for solar tracking. It highlights the system’s potential for efficient energy harvesting and ease of construction. The article emphasizes the system’s contribution to the advancement of research in solar robotics and its potential for providing a viable solution for efficient solar energy harvesting, leveraging advanced design and engineering tools such as 3D CAD, Matlab® Simulink and Matlab® Simscape.

articleTitle: Pose Estimation of a Differential-Drive Mobile Robot Using EKF-Based Sensor Fusion
abstract: Localization is an important process in navigation systems. In this stage, the robot gathers the necessary data to navigate safely and reach its destination. This paper presents a robust pose estimation method for a differential-drive robot using sensor fusion techniques, along with the design, instrumentation, and implementation in a warehouse robot used for transporting loads, focusing on real-world applications. The objective is to accurately determine the robot’s position and orientation by integrating data from wheel encoders and an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) mounted on the robot. The wheel encoders allow the estimation of the linear and angular velocities of the robot, while the IMU offers complementary data on the robot’s acceleration and angular rates. The data is fused through the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), considering the kinematics of the differential-drive robot and the uncertainties of the sensor measurements. The results from simulations and real-world experiments demonstrate an improvement in the pose estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Development and Experimental Control of a Wheeled Humanoid Robot
abstract: This article presents the electromechanical development and balance controller of a wheeled humanoid robot, with experimental tests. The objective of replacing the legs of a humanoid with a differential platform, creating an inverted pendulum, is to increase the maneuverability and the velocity of the robot movements. The prototype presented has a torso with two actuated arms that allows it to actively influence the movement of the differential platform. To verify the operation of the controller, designed by state feedback, experimental balance tests were carried out, under different conditions: translational and rotational movements, using straight and curved trajectories, on horizontal and inclined surfaces, with and without external disturbances. Furthermore, a test is presented that shows the effect of the movement of the arms on the differential platform, which is produced by the manipulation of the projection of the center of gravity.

articleTitle: Non Expensive Mobile Robot for Sensor Based Research on Artificial Cognition
abstract: Research on Embodied Cognition constantly faces two difficulties related to hardware: either robotic platforms are too expensive for the University budget and/or robots were designed for industrial purposes, favoring fine control and reproducibility at the cost of restricted customization for sensor readings and movement control. In order to fully explore new venues for machine learning algorithms linking the pathways from sensation to cognition, back to acting, the physical architecture of the robot must be open and its programming easily altered without putting humans or robots at risk. In the search for a friendly robotic environment for research on cognition, a simple architecture is presented here, with a cost around $10,000 MX or $600 US.

articleTitle: Software package for analysis and programming of experimental walks of the Bioloid humanoid robot
abstract: This article presents the SYGABIR (System for Gait Analysis of Bipedal Robots), a software package that integrates a set of computational tools aimed at analyzing the walking of the Bioloid humanoid robot. The graphical interface allows the user to perform the successive stages of computation and simulation required to obtain the joint control signals that allow the robot to walk stably in an experiment, for a given set of parameters that determine the robot’s gait. As a result of a typical walking simulation, the package displays graphs that help the user to analyze the given gait, according to different criteria. The analysis on SYGABIR is supported by dedicated tools, and other functions provided by Webots© and R+Motion. Furthermore, the interface allows the user to order the execution of the experiment or to modify the initial parameters in order to obtain a different gait. The application of the software package in a case study illustrates the usefulness of SYGABIR in research processes related to humanoid gaits.

articleTitle: Autonomous Drone Navigation using Monocular ORB-SLAM2 in Structured Environments
abstract: The present work shows and tests experimentally a methodology to perform autonomous drone navigation solely relying in visual data, based on simultaneous localization and mapping. Additionally a simple yet effective flight control law is proposed and tested, control stability analysis using Laplace transform is presented. The experiments are carried out with a low-spec commercial drone which in combination with a mediumtier laptop can asymptotically reduce the position error to 2.9 cm.

articleTitle: Stabilization of a Two-Wheeled Self-Balancing Robot Using Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This work deals with the stabilization of a two-wheeled self-balancing robot (TWSBR) and its displacement from one reference point to another by implementing a reinforcement learning (RL) scheme in conjunction with a proportional-derivative (PD) control. Conventional control schemes require either precise or partial knowledge of the system, or numerous computations. The proposed RL-based framework does not depend on any a priori knowledge of the system model. This RL-based control strategy is contrasted with a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller and an adaptive neural network (ANN) controller. Simulation results from a virtual prototype for a TWSBR, which captures the mechanical and dynamic characteristics from the real system, demonstrate that the RL-based framework exhibits an excellent performance concerning to the displacement of the TWSBR, even when an external disturbance affects to the system.

articleTitle: Implementation of PRM in a Three-Wheeled Holonomic Robot
abstract: This study details the design and construction of a three-wheeled holonomic mobile robot, emphasizing its capability to maneuver in confined spaces. The robot is built from lightweight, durable materials and features wireless communication and three omnidirectional wheels, which enable movement in any direction. A kinematic control was implemented to achieve precise navigation to desired points. The Probabilistic Roadmap (PRM) algorithm was applied for route planning in obstaclerich environments to facilitate effective obstacle avoidance. The outcome is a robot well-suited for applications in complex environments.

articleTitle: Best performance and least fragile time-delayed controllers implemented on a 3-DOF helicopter
abstract: In this paper we propose two time-delayed controllers and perform experiments for the trajectory tracking problem of a 3-DOF helicopter. Due to the choice of their gains, one of them is called best performance controller since the closed-loop system tends to a desired reference as soon as possible and the other one is called least fragile controller since the controller gains are as far as possible from the boundary of the stability region. The results are compared with a PD controller tuned using linear quadratic regulation (LQR) techniques.

articleTitle: Modeling and Preliminary Characterization of a Large Differential-Drive Mobile Robot
abstract: A comprehensive procedure is presented for deriving the kinematic and dynamic models of an electrically driven differential drive mobile robot (DDMR) with four wheels, configured in a 2:1 arrangement. The synthesis of this Lagrangian formulation, subject to non-holonomic constraints, includes the dynamics of the motors for each wheel. This model is characterized using the Turix VE 2.0 mobile robot from the Control Group Laboratory, aimed at executing arbitrary trajectories comparing it with an experimental data set based on sensor fusion from an IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit), encoder on the axis of each motor and the extended Kalman filter.The results show consistent data validating the effectiveness of the proposed modeling approach, using parameters from a real robot. Valuable insights are obtained that guide the next phase of closed-loop control, highlighting the importance of the third-order model, which integrates motor dynamics into the motion control architecture. These findings provide a foundation for the design and development of a robotic autonomous vehicle of these dimensions.

articleTitle: Exoskeleton design for patients with mobility impairments: Robotic and gait-based design
abstract: This article discusses the development of a lower limb exoskeleton designed for use by people with motor disabilities. The design of the exoskeleton incorporates the various movements of the human body, and hence the model of the robotic system is derived from human body movements. The design of the exoskeleton incorporates many methodologies from the field of robotics, including kinematic and dynamic investigations, as well as control theory. In addition, the exoskeleton’s own gait is computed through gait analysis using vision techniques.For its part, the gait analysis of the proposed work is done using vision techniques, that is, a study is carried out with patients who walk, where the different angular values of their lower limbs are extracted, and based on them apply these values to the proposed exoskeleton.

articleTitle: Controller Design for Path Following in Autonomous Vehicles with Ackerman Geometry using an LPV Approach
abstract: This paper presents the design of a convex controller for path following in autonomous vehicles with Ackerman geometry. First, the tracking error model is developed considering the lateral dynamics of the vehicle, using an LPV approach to obtain an exact convex representation. A Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) is used for the controller design. In addition, a second controller is considered to regulate the vehicle wheel’s speed, increasing the system’s performance. Finally, the developed algorithms are evaluated through simulations using data and parameters of the Rosmaster R2 mobile vehicle. The results demonstrate accurate trajectory tracking with small lateral and yaw errors, demonstrating the proposed approach’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Human-robot physical interaction system as a tool for neurocognitive stimulation in children with ADHD in Mexico
abstract: This research work promotes the use of an interactive virtual environment, with the purpose of strengthening neurocognitive stimulation in children with ADHD (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder), through a human-robot physical interaction system (HRpI); as well as establishing the conditions that allow the application of supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques that favor diagnosis. Clinical evaluation strategies in care and treatment centers for neurodivergent children are based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5); however, not using integrated technological platforms with biofeedback and neurophysiological stimulation associated with each case study, which contributes to the improvement of the clinical procedure. The proposed HRpI system is constituted by a haptic device with the human operator (patient) in the control loop. The movement instructions are designed based on a clinical protocol that evaluates hand-eye coordination, based on virtual mazes to navigate with one or two upper limbs. The platform is configured with strategies: i) passive haptic guidance and ii) active haptic exploration. In the first case, the robot guides the human in the optimal solution, correcting the interactive forces that condition the presence of disturbances, and shape the required energy; and in the second case, the human voluntarily solves the maze, which implies that the velocity and instantaneous position are variable. Kinesthetic force feedback is based on a viscoelasticity model (spring-damper system) in both haptic interaction strategies. During the development of the task, the instrumentation of brain waves are correlated with the state of the robotic system (position, velocity, energy and instantaneous errors); all this for the evaluation of performance metrics that contribute to the diagnosis. The expected result corresponds to determining the engram in terms of duration and frequency in brain plasticity for self-regulation purposes of the neurodivergent patient; as well as its impact as a value proposition to the Continuous Improvement School Program (PEMC) of basic education institutions in Mexico.

articleTitle: Scale Prototype of Pipeline Inspection Gauge for 2D Mapping
abstract: The accurate acquisition of pipeline position data is critical for the oil industry, significantly impacting maintenance strategies and operational efficiency. Traditional Pipeline Inspection Gauges (PIGs) often face challenges with data accuracy and realtime transmission, limiting their effectiveness. This study presents the development and evaluation of a PIG designed for precise pipeline mapping under controlled conditions. The PIG features flexible arms and is equipped with an ESP32 microcontroller, integrating an IMU, magnetometer, and incremental encoders. The data is processed using an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to enhance positional accuracy. Controlled tests in a PVC pipeline environment confirmed the system's consistency and reliability.The PIG achieved a distance measurement error of 0.34% and an angular error of 4.67%, with 0% data loss and low latency. The implementation of the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol with Quality of Service (QoS) level 2 ensures reliable data transmission, storing messages on the server until receipt is confirmed. Built-in connection maintenance mechanisms and automatic reconnection capabilities minimize data loss, achieving near-zero data loss under optimal conditions. Although the communication protocol was tested in ideal conditions (PVC pipes and short distances), the results demonstrate the system's potential for industrial applications, underscoring the importance of continuous calibration and energy optimization. While the controlled testing environment validates the PIG's efficiency, further testing in more diverse and realistic conditions is necessary to fully assess its reliability and performance.

articleTitle: Hamiltonian prediction as a diagnostic metric in the upper limb using assistive robotics
abstract: The dynamics of robotic systems, which involve human participation in the control loop, represent high levels of uncertainty that can not only affect the stability of the interaction system but also lead to poor performance in the robot’s task execution. Stability is considered an intervened system; it can be assessed through the measurement of the total intervened energy. To this end, a regression model is proposed for the prediction of total energy, based on the robot’s motion (position and speed) controlled with the human operator in the loop. The purpose is to verify, through energy, the level of training in patients with motor limitations. The case study focuses on a patient with Guillain-Barré syndrome, and the proposed method uses the Hamiltonian function to model the energy behavior of the system during patient interaction.

articleTitle: Haptic simulation as a tool to explain the relationships between force, field, potential and energy for point electric charges
abstract: As part of the academic training of an engineering student, the laws associated with electromagnetism represent a subject whose theory and practice represent the bases of understanding other training disciplines, alluding to electronics, telecommunications, digital and analog systems. The bases to understand the physics of electromagnetism correspond to electrostatics; to this end, the topics associated with force, field, potential and energy for point electric charges correspond to the topics addressed in this contribution. A technological platform is proposed, designed to strengthen the principles of electrostatics from visual and kinesthetic stimulation. Studies associated with neurophysiological perception, with a focus on the learning process, argue that involving a greater number of sensory channels strengthens the understanding of knowledge that typically considers conventional strategies such as presentations and blackboard management. The platform is proposed with two haptic devices whose dynamics are controlled based on the evaluation of physical laws, as well as the data modified online by the student. The virtual reality environment is based on a graphical representation of a system of electrical charges, associated with each of the end effectors of the haptic devices. To do this, Unity 3D is used as a cross-platform tool for the integration of the virtual environment; the force commands, calculated from the physical laws of electrostatics, are sent to the haptic devices from C# scripts in real time. The workload index was verified through the NASA TLX protocol, in which 10 engineering students with theoretical knowledge of electricity and magnetism were evaluated.

articleTitle: Bridging the Gap: Automated Tools for EV Charging Infrastructure Planning
abstract: This article presents an analysis of the automated calculation of stops and energy consumption for electric vehicles (EVs) using a custom Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) program integrated with Microsoft Excel. The study evaluates two EV models, the JAC E10X and Tesla Model Y, across three different routes under identical operating conditions, including passenger loads and average speeds. The analysis incorporates two scenarios: Case 1, representing an average family with a total passenger mass of 253.5 kg, and Case 2, with five adults totaling 355 kg. The program calculates whether the available battery energy is sufficient to complete each route segment and determines where additional stops for recharging are needed. Results reveal that the Tesla Model Y, with its larger battery capacity, requires significantly fewer stops than the JAC E10X. This finding highlights the impact of battery size on long-distance travel and has implications for optimizing electric vehicle infrastructure. The study also proposes the development of an advanced platform that integrates real-time data through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) to improve route and charging optimization based on vehicle specifications and passenger details.

articleTitle: Self-tuned closed-loop controller based on statistical data using a servomechanism
abstract: This work presents the application and use of statistical data for the design and proposal of a class of controller capable of self-tuning its gains automatically using statistical tools. The gain autotuning technique is based on sampling the output, obtaining the mean and standard deviation, the value of z in the central limit theorem. Subsequently, the probability level is estimated using the central limit theorem that allows mapping from the probability space to the profit space of the online self-tuned controller using a sigmoid type of function. Finally, some simulations and a real-time experiment with a servomechanism are presented.
